direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt requires a pure Node.js ESM migration for jose/test8.py, exact argparse-compatible flags, JWT output parity, local modules, .mjs suffixes, no external imports, and generated files under /output.
Parallel metadata records actual parallel use, three subagents, completed evaluation, process success, and official solution_passed false at 49 of 70 testcases.
Parallel status confirms multi-agent mode, artifact files including two overlapping module trees, protocol validity, and the current completed official evaluator result of 49/70 failed.
Parallel evaluation summary is the official completed record: evaluator ok, 70 expected cases, pass rate 0.7, solution_passed false.
Parallel final response presents the parent module hierarchy and entry file, claiming exact verification against the executable and argparse edge cases.

timeline_reviews.summary: Parallel cell trajectory mirrors the parent run: executable probing, child delegation, local implementation, waits, child interruption, copy from /workspace/output to /output, final verification, and final answer.

Parallel parent probed the executable, spawned /root/cli_probe, built an implementation in /workspace/output, waited for the child, sent a follow-up, interrupted the child, copied its own tree to /output, verified samples, and closed.

The first child acted beyond a simple probe: it spawned another CLI probe, consumed that result, wrote an independent /output implementation, ran parity tests, found a plain-hyphen payload mismatch, and was aborted before final return.
The nested child probed argparse behavior and returned a concrete CLI findings report to the first child, including required-argument errors, repeated flag behavior, and accepted forms.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is byte-identical to the parallel prompt and specifies ESM-only Node.js files in /output with exact CLI, JWT, output formatting, no external packages, and no Python calls.
Serial metadata records no parallel use, zero subagents, completed evaluation, process success, and official solution_passed false at 49 of 70 testcases.
Serial status confirms multi-agent disabled, artifact files in one module tree, no child activity, and the current completed official evaluator result of 49/70 failed.
Serial evaluation summary is the official completed record: evaluator ok, 70 expected cases, pass rate 0.7, solution_passed false.
Serial final response lists the generated /output entry and library files and claims verification of samples and several CLI parity cases.

timeline_reviews.summary: Serial cell trajectory mirrors a single-agent run: executable probes, one implementation patch to /output, local validation, sample checks, and final answer.
Serial agent directly explored argparse and JWT behavior, implemented one local module tree, tested representative samples and parser edges, and closed without delegation or shared workspace writes.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized pure ESM, .mjs output, no external dependencies, manual argv parsing, JWT encode and unverified decode behavior, Python-style printed dictionaries, and /output delivery.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership while also spawning a CLI probe child. That child spawned a nested probe, then independently wrote an /output implementation and continued verification.
parallel.implementation: The parent implemented a module tree first under /workspace/output, replaced a Web Crypto signer with a pure JS SHA-256/HMAC path, tightened some help handling, and later copied that tree to /output.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivery used a late copy from /workspace/output to /output, after the first child had already written a different /output tree. The final artifact therefore contained both parent and child module names.
parallel.verification: The parent compared sample outputs, help text, repeated options, empty values, negative-looking values, and some help quirks. A child also ran parser checks and found a plain-hyphen payload mismatch before interruption.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 21 of 70 cases. The active child did not return a final result, its implementation was overwritten, and its `--payload -` finding was not integrated.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same ESM, .mjs, /output, manual argv, no external dependency, JWT, unverified decode, and Python-style formatting requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial agent owned the entire pipeline itself: probe executable behavior, implement parser and JWT modules, write /output/test8.mjs, then verify locally.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote one module tree directly in /output, with argParser, base64url, textCodec, sha256, hmacSha256, jwt, pythonRepr, and test8.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial implementation was assembled in a single /output tree with no child output, no competing implementation tree, and no observed overwrite of another actor's deliverable.
serial.verification: The serial run checked the main sample, help and error text, abbreviations, repeated flags, empty values, negative-looking values, unknown arguments, and all provided sample vectors.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation also failed 21 of 70 cases. The exact hidden failing cases are not exposed, but the trajectory shows limited parity exploration beyond selected samples and parser cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required ESM .mjs Node migration, exact CLI behavior, no external packages, and /output delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt obligations and used the same executable-based behavioral probing approach.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference explains the score; both targeted the same JWT and argparse behavior and both failed 49/70.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split off a CLI probe child while the parent retained implementation and later spawned a nested child through the first child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept probing, implementation, verification, and final delivery in one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced overlapping ownership of executable probing and eventually implementation; serial avoided any delegated ownership boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child-task content is opaque in the raw ledger, but the observable boundary shows a CLI probe child that later wrote implementation files and reported through nested handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent handoff; all probed facts stayed in the same agent context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The important context difference is not a missing initial requirement but a later result lifecycle and workspace coordination issue around child work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote a /workspace/output tree, replaced Web Crypto with pure JS HMAC/SHA-256, then copied it into /output; the child separately wrote a different /output tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one /output tree with local parser, base64url, sha256, hmac, jwt, formatter, and entry modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementation goal was similar, but parallel produced competing implementations before final delivery while serial produced one implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited twice for the child, observed timeouts, sent a follow-up, then interrupted the still-running child before it returned a final result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and completed only after its own local verification sequence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost an active child result lifecycle; serial had no comparable unreturned delegated result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child wrote required /output files, and later the parent copied a different /workspace/output tree over /output, leaving both parent and stale child module paths in the artifact list.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and delivered one /output tree with no competing writer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a real shared-deliverable overwrite and final artifact provenance problem; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified visible sample tokens, selected parser errors, and some help quirks, but the official evaluator still failed 21 hidden cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified the visible samples and several parser cases, and also failed 21 hidden official cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verification suites were insufficient for the official hidden cases; parallel additionally failed to integrate one child-discovered edge finding before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent more requests and tokens, waited on a child twice, interrupted it, then closed after copying and verifying the parent tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial spent fewer requests and tokens, finished in one actor, and closed after local checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel coordination created extra budget use and lost child work, but did not produce a different official pass/fail relation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official records show both runs failed with the same 49/70 score. Both built pure JS ESM JWT implementations and verified visible samples plus selected CLI behavior, so the official outcome is not discordant. The parallel run has additional adverse coordination episodes, but the available evidence supports them as process damage and provenance loss rather than a proven explanation for a score difference.
parallel_contributors: Parallel child work was interrupted and not returned before closure.
Parallel final /output provenance was mixed by copying parent files over child-created deliverables.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided child lifecycle and shared-output coordination boundaries.
Serial still had insufficient hidden-case coverage and failed the same 21 official cases.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both implementations appear to match visible sample JWT outputs and selected argparse behavior but did not cover the hidden official cases.
The exact hidden failing cases are not exposed by the mounted evaluation summary.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained labels are parallel adverse process patterns, not exclusive or proven official-failure causes

candidates.reason: The parallel parent and first child both implemented code; the problem is not absence of an implementation owner.
The parent did perform final integration by copying its tree; the issue is an overwrite of another actor's deliverable, not owner absence.
The required entry file was assembled and delivered; the defect is competing writes and interrupted child work, not no assembly owner.
The parent owned end-to-end delivery and closure; failures are not from a missing pipeline owner.
Implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; parent and child work overlapped.
Investigation and implementation overlapped rather than forming a completed serial investigation phase that delayed all implementation.
The parent continued implementing and verifying the critical path; no indispensable path is shown starved by auxiliary work.
There were only a few children and the run did not time out; the adverse events are interruption and overwrite, not collective fan-out exhaustion.
The child did expand into implementation, but the directly evidenced failure is explicit interruption before return rather than a proven overbroad original assignment.
The child brief content is opaque and the child followed enough task context to probe CLI behavior and write an implementation; no known requirement omission is proven.
The observed incompatibility is not an omitted interface contract between separately owned components; it is a shared deliverable overwrite.
There is no evidence that a known fact was omitted or truncated in a handoff; the key child finding was not returned because the child was interrupted.
No oversized returned report prevented parent consumption; child outputs were either concise nested findings or not returned before interruption.
The parent is not shown consuming a handoff that described superseded workspace state.
No incompatible completed reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated; the conflict was a concrete shared-output overwrite.
The parent ran integrated local checks before final response; hidden official failure alone cannot establish unsupported global completion.
No replacement or retry child repeated prior work without inherited checkpoint state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly interrupted the active CLI probe child before it finalized and returned the plain-hyphen parser finding it had just exposed.
candidates.realized_consequence: The child-discovered `--payload -` parser edge did not reach final integration or the parent final response before closure.
candidates.near_match_reason: The child had not completed a verifier result; the parent actively stopped the child before the finding was finalized.

candidates.reason: The interrupted child did not have a complete promotable final candidate with the plain-hyphen finding resolved; interruption is the direct event.
The parent ran required-location checks after copying to /output, so the retained issue is not a post-verification merge.
A child implementation existed, but it was overwritten in the shared deliverable; the write label is more specific than missing join.
The nearest verifier-like symptom is covered by Early Child Termination because the child was explicitly interrupted before returning.
The parent was not reacting to a failed child; it explicitly interrupted a still-running child and closed with its own implementation.
The nested child's completed CLI report was consumed by the first child; the parent-level problem is not a visible completed result ignored by the parent.
The parent used list and follow-up actions around the waits and then explicitly interrupted; routine waiting is not the best classification.
The collision is not merely cross-file competing scope; the parent directly replaced the required entry deliverable and overlapping modules.
There is no evidence of live same-file merge reconciliation; the stronger evidence is wholesale copy overwrite of the deliverable.
Overlapping library sources were overwritten, but the event also replaced the required entry point, so Deliverable Overwrite has precedence.
The child wrote /output/test8.mjs and modules, then the parent copied a different tree over /output, replacing the required entry deliverable while another agent owned it.
candidates.realized_consequence: The final artifact mixed the parent's delivered entry point with stale child-created modules, obscuring provenance and discarding the child's deliverable work.
candidates.near_match_reason: Multiple final-tree files were affected, but the required executable entry point was directly replaced, so Deliverable Overwrite is more specific.

candidates.reason: The final tree was affected, but the canonical precedence chooses Deliverable Overwrite because /output/test8.mjs was directly replaced.
The workspace was shared, but a more specific deliverable overwrite is proven, so the generic unisolated-write label is not retained.
No generated fixture, cache, temporary path, or tool artifact from one actor was consumed as stable reference input by another actor.

cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and 32 Level-3 candidates were considered; no other independent adverse parallel coordination episode clears the paired retention gate.
